title: [v5.8] libnetwork/cni: set an explicit /8 prefix for lo0 on FreeBSD
body:
ifconfig used to derive the netmask from the address class, so the bare 127.0.0.1 configured the whole 127.0.0.0/8 as on-link. FreeBSD 15 dropped that handling, and an address given without a prefix is now installed with prefix length 0.

Omitting the mask is now a hard error for regular interfaces, but loopback and point-to-point interfaces are exempt, so this silently succeeds and leaves the jail's lo0 with 127.0.0.1/0 instead of 127.0.0.1/8.

Configure 127.0.0.1/8 explicitly, matching Linux and what FreeBSD 14 and older produced.

comments.body: Wait this is for 5.8? This branch is only for critical bug fixes and security fixes. CNI is unsupported by us upstream now as the code is gone on main. If @dfr prefers this to be merged I would not object but we only do new releases here when required for security updates.

It is probably better for us to add this change as a patch in the FreeBSD port for Podman rather than push it to your security branch. @b8b, can you create a problem report on bugs.freebsd.org containing the patch and I will update the port.

Longer term, we have a developer working on a Netavark port for FreeBSD and we can make sure that loopback interfaces are addressed correctly in that port.

Closing this, per @dfr's suggestion: the fix will be carried as a patch in the
FreeBSD port (sysutils/podman).

Problem report with the patch: https://bugs.freebsd.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=300656

Thanks @dfr and @Luap99.
